0:0.caption: Every program, whether it's a calculator, a chat app or a video game, is really a story about data.
0:0.spoken: Every program, whether it's a calculator, a chat app or a video game, is really a story about data.

0:1.caption: Where the data lives. What it's made of. How it changes.
0:1.spoken: Where the data lives. What it's made of. How it changes.

0:2.caption: Today we'll draw three big ideas as pictures: variables, data types, and functions.
0:2.spoken: Today we'll draw three big ideas as pictures: variables, data types, and functions.

1:1.caption: When Python runs age = 12, it first makes the value 12…
1:1.spoken: When Python runs age equals 12, it first makes the value 12...

1:2.caption: …then ties a name tag to it. A variable isn't a box. It's a label on a string.
1:2.spoken: ...then ties a name tag to it. A variable isn't a box. It's a label on a string.

1:3.caption: Now: age = age + 1. Python always works out the right-hand side first.
1:3.spoken: Now: age equals age plus 1. Python always works out the right-hand side first.

1:4.caption: 12 plus 1 makes a brand-new value, 13. Then the tag's string moves over to it.
1:4.spoken: 12 plus 1 makes a brand-new value, 13. Then the tag's string moves over to it.

1:5.caption: Nothing is tied to the 12 anymore, so Python quietly recycles it.
1:5.spoken: Nothing is tied to the 12 anymore, so Python quietly recycles it.

1:6.caption: nickname = age doesn't copy anything. It ties a second tag to the very same 13.
1:6.spoken: nickname equals age doesn't copy anything. It ties a second tag to the very same 13.

1:7.caption: Names are cheap. Values are the real things. Keep this picture; it explains a lot of Python.
1:7.spoken: Names are cheap. Values are the real things. Keep this picture; it explains a lot of Python.

2:0.caption: Chapter two: data types, or what a value is made of.
2:0.spoken: Chapter two: data types, or what a value is made of.

2:1.caption: int: whole numbers. Countable, like bricks. There's no such thing as half a brick.
2:1.spoken: integer: whole numbers. Countable, like bricks. There's no such thing as half a brick.

2:2.caption: float: numbers with a decimal point. Measured, like water in a beaker.
2:2.spoken: float: numbers with a decimal point. Measured, like water in a beaker.

2:3.caption: str: text. A string is literally a string of characters, like beads on a thread, numbered from zero.
2:3.spoken: S T R: text. A string is literally a string of characters, like beads on a thread, numbered from zero.

2:4.caption: bool: a light switch. Just two settings, True or False.
2:4.spoken: Boolean: a light switch. Just two settings, True or False.

2:5.caption: So why care? Watch the same plus sign work on two different materials.
2:5.spoken: So why care? Watch the same plus sign work on two different materials.

2:6.caption: Bricks plus bricks: 3 and 4 stack into 7.
2:6.spoken: Bricks plus bricks: 3 and 4 stack into 7.

2:7.caption: Beads plus beads: the threads get tied end to end, so "3" + "4" becomes "34".
2:7.spoken: Beads plus beads: the threads get tied end to end, so "3" plus "4" becomes "34".

2:8.caption: Mix materials, a number plus text, and Python refuses with a TypeError. It won't guess how to glue a brick to a bead.
2:8.spoken: Mix materials, a number plus text, and Python refuses with a type error. It won't guess how to glue a brick to a bead.

3:0.caption: Chapter three: functions, the little factories.
3:0.spoken: Chapter three: functions, the little factories.

3:1.caption: def builds a machine called double. Nothing runs yet. It's a blueprint with a name.
3:1.spoken: def builds a machine called double. Nothing runs yet. It's a blueprint with a name.

3:2.caption: The machine has one input slot, labelled x, and one job: multiply by two.
3:2.spoken: The machine has one input slot, labelled x, and one job: multiply by two.

3:3.caption: Calling double(3) drops a 3 into the hopper…
3:3.spoken: Calling double(3) drops a 3 into the hopper...

3:4.caption: …where it gets a temporary name tag, x. The gears turn: x times 2…
3:4.spoken: ...where it gets a temporary name tag, x. The gears turn: x times 2...

3:5.caption: …and return sends the result out of the chute. double(3) gives back 6.
3:5.spoken: ...and return sends the result out of the chute. double(3) gives back 6.

3:6.caption: Same machine, different material. Let's feed it the string "ha".
3:6.spoken: Same machine, different material. Let's feed it the string "ha".

3:7.caption: A string times 2 repeats the text. Out comes "haha".
3:7.spoken: A string times 2 repeats the text. Out comes "haha".

3:8.caption: Write the recipe once, use it forever. That's the whole point of a function.
3:8.spoken: Write the recipe once, use it forever. That's the whole point of a function.

4:1.caption: Here's a second machine. shout takes a word, makes it uppercase, and adds an exclamation mark.
4:1.spoken: Here's a second machine. shout takes a word, makes it uppercase, and adds an exclamation mark.

4:2.caption: Now nest them. Python works inside out: the innermost call runs first.
4:2.spoken: Now nest them. Python works inside out: the innermost call runs first.

4:3.caption: "hi" goes into double and comes out as "hihi"…
4:3.spoken: "hi" goes into double and comes out as "hihi"...

4:4.caption: …which rolls straight into shout. Out comes "HIHI!"
4:4.spoken: ...which rolls straight into shout. Out comes "hi hi!"

4:5.caption: Finally, result = ties a name tag to the finished product. We're back at chapter one.
4:5.spoken: Finally, result equals ties a name tag to the finished product. We're back at chapter one.

4:6.caption: That's secretly what every big program is: small, well-named machines, wired into assembly lines.
4:6.spoken: That's secretly what every big program is: small, well-named machines, wired into assembly lines.

5:1.caption: Variables are name tags tied to values.
5:1.spoken: Variables are name tags tied to values.

5:2.caption: Types are the material a value is made of, and the material decides the rules.
5:2.spoken: Types are the material a value is made of, and the material decides the rules.

5:3.caption: Functions are machines: values go in, get transformed, and come out.
5:3.spoken: Functions are machines: values go in, get transformed, and come out.

5:4.caption: Your turn: build a machine called greet that turns "Ada" into "Hello, Ada!". You already know every piece you need.
5:4.spoken: Your turn: build a machine called greet that turns "Ada" into "Hello, Ada!". You already know every piece you need.

5:5.caption: Next episode: loops and decisions. See you there.
5:5.spoken: Next episode: loops and decisions. See you there.
